---
title: "Installing Flux"
subtitle: "One line in a terminal, then a short setup window"
---

# Install

Paste this into a terminal:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://fluxsci.github.io/install.sh | bash
```

It works on **macOS** (Apple Silicon and Intel) and **Debian/Ubuntu Linux** (x86-64), and it:

1. downloads the latest Flux release from GitHub and checks it against the release's
   published SHA-256 checksums (nothing is installed if they differ);
2. installs it: on macOS, `Flux.app` goes into `/Applications` (or `~/Applications` if
   `/Applications` isn't writable); on Linux, the `.deb` is installed with `apt`, which asks
   for your password;
3. adds `~/.local/bin` to your `PATH` with one marked line in `~/.zshrc` (or `~/.bashrc`), so
   the `flux` command works in new terminals;
4. opens Flux.

This is the one supported way to install Flux. A terminal line instead of a download button
is deliberate: Flux is not signed with an Apple Developer ID, and macOS flags apps downloaded
by a browser as from an "unidentified developer". Files fetched by `curl` carry no such flag,
so Flux simply opens. You can [read the script](https://github.com/fluxsci/flux/blob/main/install.sh)
before running it.

To install a specific release: `curl -fsSL https://fluxsci.github.io/install.sh | bash -s -- --version v0.2.0`.

## Updating

Flux checks for a new release at most once a day (Settings can turn this off). On macOS,
**Update now** runs the same installer: it waits for Flux to quit, replaces the app and opens
it again. On Linux, Flux shows the install line to paste into a terminal, because `apt` needs
your password. Running the install line again at any time also updates Flux.

## Uninstalling

Delete `/Applications/Flux.app` (macOS) or run `sudo apt remove flux` (Linux). Your projects
are never touched. Flux's machine-level files live in `~/FluxConfig` (your context, FluxLib
and global plot library: keep these if you might come back) and `~/.local/share/flux`; the
installer's PATH line is the one under `# Added by Flux` in your shell startup file.

# First launch: the setup window

The first time Flux opens, a short **Set up Flux** window lists the optional extras. Each
row checks what is already on the machine and offers one button for what's missing; nothing
needs admin rights or a terminal. Reopen it any time from **Settings → General → Setup** or
the command palette (**Ctrl+K → Set up Flux…**).

| Row | What it gives you | What the button does |
|---|---|---|
| **`flux` in the terminal** | the `flux` command for you and your AI agents | installs the launcher and puts `~/.local/bin` on your PATH (the installer usually did this already) |
| **Word export · Quarto** | Word export and `flux compile` | installs [Quarto](https://quarto.org) into `~/FluxConfig` (a Quarto you already have always wins) |
| **PDF through Quarto · TinyTeX** | PDFs built by Quarto (`flux compile --to pdf`, journal styles) | installs TinyTeX through Quarto, in your home folder |
| **Plots** | semantic, restylable plots | nothing to install in Flux: add **fluxplot** to your analysis environment (below) |
| **AI agents** | Claude Code or Codex working inside your projects | detects them, links to their installers, and connects them to Flux |

Everything else ships inside the app, including Flux's own PDF export, its video encoder,
the local writing-correction model and the offline help.

# The companions in detail

## fluxplot (your plots)

[fluxplot](https://github.com/fluxsci/fluxplot) lives in **your own analysis
environment**, beside the rest of your Python stack, not inside Flux. Flux runs each plot's
recipe with the command recorded in it, in that environment. With
[uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) (recommended; agents set up a uv project per analysis):

```bash
uv add fluxplot            # in an analysis project (uv init first if it is new)
uv add "fluxplot[mesh]"    # also the 3D mesh exports
```

or `pip install fluxplot` in any other environment.

Why it matters: fluxplot emits *semantic* SVGs. Every series, point, and axis label carries
a stable id, which is what makes Flux figures restylable per part, regenerable without losing
hand-tuning, and morphable in slides. Without it, plots import as plain images.

## Quarto + TinyTeX (Word export and `flux compile`)

Flux's own PDF export needs neither. Quarto powers Word export and `flux compile` (HTML,
Word, PDF; it bundles its own pandoc), and Quarto's PDF builds additionally need TeX. The
setup window installs both. If you prefer to manage them yourself, install Quarto from
[quarto.org](https://quarto.org) (or `brew install --cask quarto`); Flux always uses a Quarto
you installed (on your `PATH` or in its usual install folder) before its own copy, and
`quarto install tinytex` adds TeX. Without TeX, `flux compile --to pdf` fails while HTML and
Word still work.

**TinyTeX is not added to your PATH.** It installs into `~/Library/TinyTeX` (macOS) or
`~/.TinyTeX` (Linux). Flux and Quarto find it anyway, but TeX's own commands (`tlmgr`,
`kpsewhich`, used below) need it on your PATH:

```bash
# macOS — add to ~/.zshrc to make it permanent
export PATH="$HOME/Library/TinyTeX/bin/universal-darwin:$PATH"
# Linux — add to ~/.bashrc
export PATH="$HOME/.TinyTeX/bin/x86_64-linux:$PATH"
```

### Extras for journal-styled PDF

Exporting with a journal style (Nature, say) asks LaTeX for things a minimal
install may not have: **line numbers**, **double spacing**, a **Times-compatible
font**, and a way to place Flux's SVG figures in a PDF. How you add them depends
on how TeX got onto the machine:

| TeX install | Command | Needs admin? |
|---|---|---|
| TinyTeX (the setup window, or `quarto install tinytex`) | `tlmgr install lineno setspace` | No — TinyTeX lives in your home directory |
| MacTeX | `sudo tlmgr install lineno setspace` | Yes |
| Linux distro TeX Live (apt) | `sudo apt install texlive-latex-recommended texlive-humanities texlive-luatex texlive-fonts-recommended` | Yes — Debian and Ubuntu disable `tlmgr` package installs |

Figures also need **`rsvg-convert`** (`librsvg2-bin` on Debian and Ubuntu,
`librsvg` on Homebrew and Arch): Flux renders figures as SVG, and LaTeX cannot
place those directly.

Check what you have (both `tlmgr` and `kpsewhich` need TinyTeX on your PATH — see above):

```bash
kpsewhich lineno.sty setspace.sty   # both should print a path
rsvg-convert --version              # needed for figures in PDF
```

None of this affects **Word**, which is what Nature prefers for submission
anyway — a journal-styled `.docx` needs no TeX at all. When an export does hit a
missing piece, Flux names the package to install instead of showing you the raw
LaTeX log.

## Fonts

Fluxplot saves plot text as *real text*, and Flux rasterizes figures with the fonts
installed on the machine. The house style's stacks lead with **Arial / Helvetica**
(sans) and **Georgia / Times New Roman / Latin Modern** (serif), falling back to DejaVu.

- **macOS**: Arial, Helvetica, Georgia, Times New Roman are system fonts — you're
  covered. (DejaVu is *not* present; avoid relying on it in cross-machine workflows.)
- **Linux**: install the MS core fonts (`ttf-mscorefonts-installer` on Debian/Ubuntu) or
  accept the DejaVu look. Latin Modern comes with TeX (`fonts-lmodern`).
- **Rule of thumb**: keep the *generating* machine and the *rendering* machine font-
  consistent — matplotlib embeds whichever family it actually picked, and the renderer
  substitutes anything missing, which shifts text metrics subtly.

# Your FluxConfig

Launching Flux (or a CLI command) initializes `~/FluxConfig`: your **UserContext**,
the stock **FluxContext** manual, and the **FluxLib** reference library. Your personal
context is seeded once; the stock manual is refreshed with this installation's paths.

Flux creates stable `flux` and `flux-connect` launchers in `~/.local/share/flux/bin`
(Linux/macOS), or `%LOCALAPPDATA%\flux\bin` (Windows), plus convenience shims in
`~/.local/bin` (which the installer puts on your PATH). Your own unmarked files there are
preserved. The only shell startup change is the installer's (or the setup window's) one
marked PATH line.

The launcher stays with its owning installation. Use **AI status → Use this Flux for
agents**, or setup's `--use-this-install`, to choose another (for example a source
checkout).

1. Fill out `~/FluxConfig/Context/UserContext/WHO-AM-I.md`.
2. Adjust `UserContext/RULES.md` and add reusable procedures under `UserContext/Skills/`.
3. Moving machines? Copy your UserContext (including Skills), FluxLib and global
   `plot_library/`. FluxContext is regenerated; run agent setup on the new machine.

See [Your context and your project's](agents/context.qmd) before opening older projects
that need migration.

# Connect an AI agent

Install and sign in to Claude Code or Codex in its own app or terminal. Open **AI** in
the titlebar, or **Ctrl+K → AI status**, then choose **Connect** on its card (the setup
window's **AI agents** row and the Home screen's **Connect an AI agent** card open the same
monitor). Review replacements if shown, then restart open agent sessions. In Codex, review
newly installed hooks in **/hooks**. This registers tools and skills; it does not start a
project session.

From a terminal the equivalent is `flux connect setup --dry-run`, then `flux connect
setup`, followed by `flux connect doctor`. Copy the panel's `/flux-connect <project>`
or `$flux-connect <project>` command into your agent to connect a session. See
[Working with AI agents](agents/connect.qmd) for the reading plan, receipt and status rows.

# Verify the setup

```bash
flux version                             # the installed build
flux config                              # machine paths + build info
flux connect doctor                      # checks the Flux AI Bundle
quarto check                             # if you export papers: quarto + tinytex
uv run python -c "import fluxplot"       # inside an analysis project
```

# Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause → fix |
|---|---|
| `flux: command not found` | Open a new terminal (the PATH line applies to new shells). Still missing → **Set up Flux… → `flux` in the terminal** |
| `compile --to pdf` fails; html works | No TeX → **Set up Flux… → PDF through Quarto**, or `quarto install tinytex` |
| Journal PDF fails with `File 'lineno.sty' not found` (or `setspace.sty`) | Minimal TeX install → the journal-PDF table above |
| Journal PDF fails mentioning `rsvg-convert` | SVG figures cannot be placed → install `librsvg2-bin` / `librsvg` |
| Journal PDF fails with `luaotfload` or `not loadable: Metric` | lualatex present but its fonts are not → `texlive-luatex` + `texlive-fonts-recommended`, or use TinyTeX |
| Plots import as flat images; `restyle` finds no parts | Plot not saved via `fp.save` (or fluxplot missing) → check `flux validate-plot` |
| Figure PNGs render with wrong/shifted text | Missing fonts on this machine → install the stacks above; keep machines consistent |
| Agent has no Flux tools or skill | Run `flux connect doctor`, use **AI status → Repair**, then restart the agent session |
| Nothing live-reloads in the open app | Watcher failed to start (a toast said so at open) → reopen the project |
| Flux "won't start" — no window, no error | A windowless earlier instance is holding the single-instance lock → `pgrep -af Flux` to find it, then `kill <pid>` (plain SIGTERM saves unsaved work on the way out; keep `kill -9` as the last resort) |
| The installer says "checksum mismatch" | A corrupted or intercepted download; nothing was installed → run it again |

# For developers: running from source

Contributors run Flux from a checkout instead (Node ≥ 22.15 required):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/fluxsci/flux ~/flux
cd ~/flux
npm ci
node node_modules/electron/install.js   # Electron 43 no longer downloads itself at install
npm run electron:dev                    # Vite dev server + Electron, hot reload
```

A checkout's launcher pins the Node it was set up with; use **AI status → Use this Flux for
agents** to point your agents at it rather than at an installed Flux. A checkout is also
required for [**Lighttable**](lighttable.qmd), the image-set triage companion, which isn't
bundled into releases. `docs/for_agents/claude-install-flux-mac.md` is a step-by-step runbook
an AI agent can follow to set up a development Mac.
